A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fair Minimum Labeling work. All 17 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-source classification experiments, Barabási–Albert runtime and coverage experiments, and Pokec scalability results in Section 6.

after.justification: v3 reports original multi-source classification results, relaxation-parameter sensitivity results and comparisons on Pokec in Section 6 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: v3 adds SPT-FML, replacing the FRT reduction with a shortest-path tree, pruning uncolored leaves and labeling the selected subtree directly. It also revises the bicriteria procedure to bucket after balanced pairwise merges and select root states using explicit relaxed quotas, rather than v1's node-level bucketing description.

E1.justification: The principal coverage remains synthetic multi-source learning on random geometric graphs, Barabási–Albert graphs and gender-grouped Pokec. However, v1's explicit central-versus-peripheral terminal scenarios are no longer reported as such; v3 fixes a corner terminal for the learning experiment. Changes to graph sizes, source counts and quotas otherwise concern evaluation settings.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds PD–STRICT, PD–MATCHED and COVERING STEINER to the learning comparison; Table 3 also compares against both primal–dual variants on Pokec. CLOSEST and ALTERNATING remain, and GREEDY corresponds to GROUP-AGNOSTIC. The Barabási–Albert sensitivity comparison no longer includes the full-DP comparator used in v1.

E3.justification: v1 charges learning baselines the sum of source-to-terminal hop distances; v3 counts selected tree edges once for every method and distinguishes strict from matched relaxed quotas. Pokec changes from a 201,900-edge sample with full coverage to a 262,846-edge prepared graph, four sizes and half-coverage targets. The sensitivity study changes from raw bucketing epsilon to controlled end-to-end relaxation with fixed graph/tree comparisons.

E4.justification: v3 replaces the exact-versus-bicriteria runtime/coverage analysis with relaxation sweeps measuring runtime, retained DP states, cost and coverage for both FRT and SPT. It adds colored-core pruning measurements and a detailed runtime breakdown. v1's central/peripheral-terminal robustness result and empirical tree-height guarantee check are removed.

E5.justification: Ten-run evaluation is retained, while paired trials and paired random seeds are now explicitly documented. v3 Table 1 reports coverage and accuracy as means without v1's standard deviations; the revised sensitivity table likewise reports mean reductions without uncertainty. Runtime and cost retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: The empirical results are extensively replaced and expanded. v1 Table 1 reports FMLAPPROX cost 74.3 and CLOSEST cost 224.0; v3 reports FRT–FULL 75.3, CLOSEST 118.2 and newly evaluated PD–STRICT 68.0. New Pokec Table 3 reports 20,000-node runtimes of 13.58 s for SPT–BOUNDED and 50.80 s for FRT–BOUNDED. Changed accounting, hardware and quotas prevent interpreting cross-version differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds the single-terminal equivalence to rooted Covering Steiner and replaces v1's one-group Set Cover reduction with new reductions establishing hardness in the number of groups. It adds constant-group approximation and APX-hardness results, corrects the ML/MSL specialization in Appendix A, and replaces the height-based bicriteria proof with merge-depth analysis. FRT projection and resource-bound proofs are also substantially revised.

C1.justification: v1 claims logarithmic hardness matched by best-possible expected-cost guarantees. v3 instead distinguishes growing-group hardness from constant-factor approximability for fixed groups and emphasizes the Covering Steiner equivalence, exactness on tree inputs, controlled coverage relaxation and the new SPT method. This substantially redefines the headline contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains that temporal constraints collapse to static connectivity for one terminal, including a qualification in Appendix B. It distinguishes SPT's instance-dependent stretch from FRT guarantees and interprets scalability through pruning and avoided embedding/projection overhead. Conversely, v1's specific discussion of fixed memberships, adaptive fairness thresholds and unmodeled individual or temporal fairness is omitted.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents eight training examples per source, validation proportion, stopping patience, test-set sizes, deterministic graph preparation and tree tie-breaking. The reported environment changes from Python 3.9/PyTorch 2.5.1 on a 96-GB Xeon node to Python 3.13 on a 32-GB i5 machine. The code pointer changes from fml to fml_code. Newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v1 describes FML as resembling Set Cover and Steiner Tree while requiring different machinery. v3 identifies exact equivalence to Covering Steiner and substantially develops its relationship to group Steiner, k-MST and existing approximation bounds. It explicitly acknowledges stronger inherited hardness and better constant-group approximation guarantees, repositioning its algorithms around tree exactness and controlled coverage–speed tradeoffs.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, combinatorial positioning, algorithm exposition, experimental narrative and appendix proofs are extensively rewritten. Section 4 gains separate structural and complexity subsections, Sections 5–6 are reorganized, the standalone Limitations section disappears and the conclusion is shortened. These are substantial narrative changes beyond renaming and renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is retained, but the experimental presentation is rebuilt. Table 1 groups methods by coverage requirements, combines group columns and adds an accuracy-gap column. v1's two-panel Figure 2 disappears in favor of a different sensitivity table, and its small Pokec table becomes a multi-method, multi-size table with cost and coverage. Algorithm displays are also revised.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves the paper by repairing central hardness and bicriteria arguments, acknowledging the established Covering Steiner relationship and replacing the unsupported tightness narrative with qualified guarantees. Consistent edge-cost accounting and relevant baselines under matched quotas also make the empirical conclusions more credible. These foundational gains outweigh reduced uncertainty reporting and omitted conceptual limitations. The abstract's broad cost-superiority claim nevertheless remains stronger than the comparisons in Table 1 support.
